nodes.summary: Let $L > 1$ and $k > 1$ be natural numbers and let $\kappa$ assign a shift $\kappa(j, n) \in \mathbb{Z}/L\mathbb{Z}$ to each $j \in \{1, \dots, k-1\}$ and each $n \ge 0$. For every $n \ge 0$, the block $A_n$ of the $(L, k, \kappa)$-Thue–Morse sequence has exactly $k^n$ letters.
nodes.title: Length of the generalized Thue–Morse blocks

nodes.summary: Let $L > 1$ and $k > 1$ be natural numbers and let $\kappa$ assign a shift $\kappa(j, n) \in \mathbb{Z}/L\mathbb{Z}$ to each $j \in \{1, \dots, k-1\}$ and each $n \ge 0$. For every $n \ge 0$, the block $A_n$ of the $(L, k, \kappa)$-Thue–Morse sequence is a prefix of $A_{n+1}$: there is a word $w$ with $A_{n+1} = A_n w$.
nodes.title: Each generalized Thue–Morse block is a prefix of the next

nodes.summary: Let $L > 1$ and $k > 1$ be natural numbers and let $\kappa$ assign a shift $\kappa(j, n) \in \mathbb{Z}/L\mathbb{Z}$ to each $j \in \{1, \dots, k-1\}$ and each $n \ge 0$. For all natural numbers $m \le n$, the block $A_m$ of the $(L, k, \kappa)$-Thue–Morse sequence is a prefix of $A_n$: there is a word $w$ with $A_n = A_m w$.
nodes.title: The generalized Thue–Morse blocks form a chain of prefixes

nodes.summary: Let $L > 1$ and $k > 1$ be natural numbers, take the letters $0, 1, \dots, L-1$ (the elements of $\mathbb{Z}/L\mathbb{Z}$), and let $\kappa$ assign a shift $\kappa(j, n) \in \mathbb{Z}/L\mathbb{Z}$ to each $j \in \{1, \dots, k-1\}$ and each $n \ge 0$. For a word $w$ and $t \in \mathbb{Z}/L\mathbb{Z}$, let $f^t(w)$ be the word obtained from $w$ by adding $t$ modulo $L$ to every letter. The blocks $A_n$ of the…
nodes.title: Blocks of the generalized Thue–Morse sequence

nodes.summary: The classical Thue–Morse block $A_0$ is the one-letter word $0$.
nodes.title: Classical Thue–Morse block of order 0

nodes.summary: The classical Thue–Morse block $A_1$ is the word $01$.
nodes.title: Classical Thue–Morse block of order 1

nodes.summary: The classical Thue–Morse block $A_2$ is the word $0110$.
nodes.title: Classical Thue–Morse block of order 2

nodes.summary: The classical Thue–Morse block $A_3$ is the word $01101001$.
nodes.title: Classical Thue–Morse block of order 3

nodes.summary: The classical Thue–Morse blocks are the blocks $A_n$ of the $(2, 2, \kappa)$-Thue–Morse sequence with $\kappa(1, n) = 1$ for every $n \ge 0$. Thus $A_0$ is the one-letter word $0$, and $A_{n+1}$ is $A_n$ followed by the word obtained from $A_n$ by exchanging the letters $0$ and $1$.
nodes.title: Classical Thue–Morse blocks

nodes.summary: Let $A_\infty$ be the infinite word of the $(2, 2, \kappa)$-Thue–Morse sequence with $\kappa(1, n) = 1$ for every $n \ge 0$. The letters of $A_\infty$ at positions $0, 1, \dots, 7$ are $0, 1, 1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1$, so $A_\infty$ begins with $01101001$.
nodes.title: The classical Thue–Morse word begins with 01101001

nodes.summary: The classical shift schedule is the map $\kappa$ that assigns to the index $j = 1$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ the letter $\kappa(1, n) = 1$ of the alphabet $\{0, 1\}$. It is the schedule of the classical Thue–Morse sequence, the $(L, k, \kappa)$-Thue–Morse sequence with $L = k = 2$.
nodes.title: Classical shift schedule

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the classical Thue–Morse block $A_n$ (the block $A_n$ of the $(L, k, \kappa)$-Thue–Morse sequence with $L = k = 2$ and $\kappa(1, i) = 1$ for all $i \in \mathbb{N}$) has exactly $2^n$ letters.
nodes.title: Length of the classical Thue–Morse blocks

nodes.summary: Let $l_1$ and $l_2$ be lists over a type, and let $m$ be a natural number less than the length of $l_1$. Then the entry at position $m$ of the concatenation of $l_1$ followed by $l_2$ equals the entry at position $m$ of $l_1$ (positions start at $0$).
nodes.title: Indexing into a concatenation

nodes.summary: Let $L, k \ge 2$, let $\kappa : \{1, \dots, k-1\} \times \mathbb{N} \to \{0, \dots, L-1\}$ be a shift schedule, and let $A_0, A_1, \dots$ be the blocks and $A_\infty$ the infinite word of the $(L, k, \kappa)$-Thue–Morse sequence. For all $m, N \in \mathbb{N}$ with $m + 1 \le N$ and $m$ less than the length of $A_N$, the letter at position $m$ of $A_N$ equals the letter at position $m$ of $A_\infty$ (positions start…
nodes.title: Later blocks agree with the infinite word

nodes.summary: Let $L, k \ge 2$, let $\kappa : \{1, \dots, k-1\} \times \mathbb{N} \to \{0, \dots, L-1\}$ be a shift schedule, and let $A_0, A_1, \dots$ be the blocks of the $(L, k, \kappa)$-Thue–Morse sequence. The infinite word $A_\infty$ over the alphabet $\{0, \dots, L-1\}$ has, for every $m \in \mathbb{N}$, as its letter at position $m$ (positions start at $0$) the letter at position $m$ of the block $A_{m+1}$, which has…
nodes.title: The infinite generalized Thue–Morse word

nodes.summary: Let $l$ be a list of lists over a type and let $m \in \mathbb{N}$. If every list in $l$ has length $m$, then the concatenation of the lists in $l$ has length $n \cdot m$, where $n$ is the number of lists in $l$.
nodes.title: Length of a concatenation of equal-length lists

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k > 1$ and every $m \in \mathbb{N}$, we have $m < k^{m+1}$.
nodes.title: A crude exponential bound

nodes.summary: For every $L \in \mathbb{N}$ and all letters $a, t$ of the alphabet $\{0, \dots, L-1\}$, the cyclic shift of $a$ by $t$ is the letter $(a + t) \bmod L$.
nodes.title: Value of the cyclic letter shift

nodes.summary: For $L \in \mathbb{N}$ and letters $a, t$ of the alphabet $\{0, \dots, L-1\}$, the cyclic shift of $a$ by $t$ is the letter $(a + t) \bmod L$. Writing the letters as $a_0, \dots, a_{L-1}$, it sends $a_i$ to $a_{(i + t) \bmod L}$.
nodes.title: Cyclic letter shift

nodes.summary: For every $L \in \mathbb{N}$, every letter $t$ of the alphabet $\{0, \dots, L-1\}$ and every finite word $w$ over that alphabet, the word obtained from $w$ by shifting each letter cyclically by $t$ has the same length as $w$.
nodes.title: Cyclic shifting preserves word length

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a natural number and let $t$ and $b$ be letters of the alphabet $\{0, 1, \dots, L - 1\}$. For a letter $a$ write $\sigma_t(a) = (a + t) \bmod L$ for its cyclic shift by $t$, and for a word $w$ over this alphabet write $\sigma_t(w)$ for the word obtained by shifting each letter of $w$. Then $b$ occurs in $\sigma_t(w)$ if and only if $b = \sigma_t(a)$ for some letter $a$ occurring in $w$.
nodes.title: Letters of a cyclically shifted word

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a natural number and let $t$ be a letter of the alphabet $\{0, 1, \dots, L - 1\}$. The cyclic shift by $t$ of a word $w = a_1 a_2 \cdots a_n$ over this alphabet is the word $\sigma_t(a_1) \sigma_t(a_2) \cdots \sigma_t(a_n)$ of the same length, where $\sigma_t(a) = (a + t) \bmod L$ is the cyclic shift of a letter.
nodes.title: Cyclic shift of a word

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be the Thue–Morse substitution, $\sigma(0) = 01$ and $\sigma(1) = 10$, applied to finite words over $\{0, 1\}$ letter by letter. For a natural number $n$, the $n$th Thue–Morse block is the finite word $\sigma^n(0)$: the $0$th block is the one-letter word $0$, and the $(n+1)$st block is obtained from the $n$th by replacing each letter $a$ with $\sigma(a)$.
nodes.title: Thue–Morse blocks

nodes.summary: The Thue–Morse substitution $\sigma$ on the alphabet $\{0, 1\}$ sends each letter to a word of length two: $\sigma(0) = 01$ and $\sigma(1) = 10$.
nodes.title: Thue–Morse substitution

nodes.summary: The Thue–Morse sequence $t_0 t_1 t_2 \cdots$ over $\{0, 1\}$ is indexed from $0$, and $t_n = 1$ exactly when the binary expansion of $n$ has an odd number of digits equal to $1$; otherwise $t_n = 0$.
nodes.title: Thue–Morse sequence

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
